from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        lecture_lines = [

        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Language of Binary", lecture_lines)

        self.place_at_grid(computer_icon, "A3", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.add(computer_icon)

        # Binary display: 3 bits
        bits = VGroup(*[Text("0", color=GREY, font_size=48) for _ in range(3)])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        # Indicate powers
        powers = VGroup(*[Text(p, color=BLUE, font_size=20) for p in ["4", "2", "1"]])
        # FIX: Adjusted position to C3 and scale 0.9
        self.place_at_grid(powers, "C3", scale_factor=0.9)
        powers.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.6)

        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        # Update text content safely
        bits[0].become(Text("1", color=YELLOW, font_size=48).move_to(bits[0].get_center()))
        bits[1].become(Text("0", color=GREY, font_size=48).move_to(bits[1].get_center()))
        bits[2].become(Text("1", color=YELLOW, font_size=48).move_to(bits[2].get_center()))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        self.place_at_grid(counter_icon, "A5", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.add(counter_icon)
        
        decimal_val = Text("Value: 5", color=WHITE, font_size=32)
        # FIX: Adjusted position to D3
        self.place_at_grid(decimal_val, "D3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(decimal_val))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Towers of Hanoi Challenge", [
            "Three rods hold disks of varying sizes.",
            "Move one disk at a time.",
            "Never place larger on smaller disks."
        ])
        
        # Load assets
        rod_path = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/rod.svg"
        disk_path = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/disk.svg"
        
        # Setup initial state of disks and pegs
        pegs = VGroup(*[SVGMobject(rod_path) for _ in range(3)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=1.0)
        
        disks = VGroup(*[SVGMobject(disk_path) for _ in range(3)])
        # Stacked by size (scaled)
        for i, disk in enumerate(disks):
            disk.scale(0.5 + i * 0.2)
            
        disks.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.05)
        
        # Position disks on first peg
        for disk in disks:
            disk.next_to(pegs[0].get_bottom(), UP, buff=0.05)
            
        self.add(pegs, disks)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_in_area(pegs, "B3", "E5", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        # Animate moving top disk
        top_disk = disks[-1]
        self.place_in_area(pegs, "B4", "E6", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(top_disk.animate.move_to(pegs[2].get_bottom() + UP*0.05))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(RED)
        self.place_in_area(pegs, "B2", "D5", scale_factor=0.75)
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application: The Cosmic Clock", [
            "64 disks take forever to move.",
            "Exponential growth outpaces linear growth.",
            "Complexity scales with binary counting."
        ])
        
        # Asset path
        clock_path = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/clock.svg"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Draw circular clock using SVG
        clock = SVGMobject(clock_path, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(clock, "D4", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Creating a hand for the SVG clock
        clock_hand = Line(ORIGIN, UP * 0.8, color=YELLOW)
        clock_hand.move_to(clock.get_center(), aligned_edge=DOWN)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(clock), GrowFromCenter(clock_hand))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Exponential growth: Hare vs Turtle
        hare = Dot(color=RED, radius=0.15)
        turtle = Dot(color=GREEN, radius=0.15)
        self.place_at_grid(hare, "F2", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(turtle, "F5", scale_factor=0.5)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(hare), FadeIn(turtle))
        self.play(
            hare.animate.shift(RIGHT * 2),
            turtle.animate.shift(RIGHT * 1),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.lecture[1].set_color(RED)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Clock hand rotating representing binary complexity
        self.play(Rotate(clock_hand, angle=PI, about_point=clock.get_center()), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: Binary Counting and the Towers of Hanoi: The Logic of Movement
outline.target_audience: High school students or introductory computer science learners

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Language of Binary
sections.content: Briefly introduce binary as a base-2 system using only 0 and 1. Explain that just as decimal (base-10) uses powers of 10, binary uses powers of 2. Use a visual representation of 3 light bulbs (representing 4, 2, and 1) to show how any number can be formed.
sections.example: Visual: 3 bulbs. If the 4-bulb and 1-bulb are ON (101), the value is 5. If all are ON (111), the value is 7.

sections.title: The Towers of Hanoi Challenge
sections.content: Introduce the puzzle: 3 rods and N disks of different sizes. Rules: Only one disk moved at a time; a larger disk cannot sit on a smaller one. Pose the question: What is the minimum number of moves to solve it for 3 disks?
sections.example: Animation: A robotic arm moving disks from Rod A to Rod C, following the rules.

sections.title: Connecting Moves to Binary Counting
sections.content: Reveal the magic link: As you count in binary (1, 2, 3, 4...), the changes in binary digits correspond exactly to disk movements. The bit that changes tells you which disk to move. If the 1st bit changes, move disk 1; if the 2nd bit changes, move disk 2.
sections.example: Table: Count 001 (Move Disk 1), 010 (Move Disk 2), 011 (Move Disk 1), 100 (Move Disk 3).

sections.title: The Power of 2^n - 1
sections.content: Explain why the total moves for 'n' disks is always 2^n - 1. Connect this back to the binary counting limit: a 3-bit binary number can count up to 7 (2^3 - 1).
sections.example: Visual: For 3 disks, 2^3 - 1 = 7 moves. Animation shows the binary counter ticking from 001 to 111 as the disks reach the target rod.

sections.title: Application: The Cosmic Clock
sections.content: Apply the concept to a real-world scale. Mention the Legend of Brahma: 64 golden disks. Calculate the time required to finish (at 1 move per second, it would take over 500 billion years). This highlights the exponential nature of binary growth.
sections.example: Animation: A turtle and a hare. The hare (exponential growth) quickly outpaces the turtle (linear growth) as the number of disks increases.
